thread:
Sophie R: FYI customer reported duplicate final tokens + doubled billing after reconnecting an SSE stream. They say final sentence repeated twice and charged twice. Repro steps attached below.

Ajay P: Can you drop the headers + raw SSE events? timing between disconnect and reconnect matters.

Sophie R: Paste from customer logs:
```
> SSE EVENT: event: token
data: {"token_index": 0, "text": "Hello"}
> SSE EVENT: event: token
data: {"token_index": 1, "text": " world"}
> CONNECTION: TCP reset by client (no FIN)
> RECONNECT: new ws/sse open with resume_token=rt-abc123, idempotency-key: ik-789
> SSE EVENT: event: token
data: {"token_index": 1, "text": " world"}
> SSE EVENT: event: token
data: {"token_index": 2, "text": "!"}
> SSE EVENT: event: done
data: {"status":"completed"}
```
They highlighted token_index 1 repeated. They used our client lib v0.9.2. Latency spike ~504s before disconnect.

Ken L: This looks like a heartbeat/ACK mismatch. If the client drops the TCP connection without ACKing the last chunk and then reconnects with a resume_token pointing to the last acknowledged offset (which in their case is stale), our resume path may re-emit tokens starting from that offset. If runtime doesn't correlate resume_token + idempotency-key it can produce overlapping emissions.

Maria C: Customer insists they sent `Idempotency-Key: ik-789` on both initial request and reconnect. They expect server to detect duplicates and not re-generate. Also note: billing events we emit on `done` and on chunk emission for certain customers (per config), so duplicates cause double bill.

Ajay P: Important: does our resume flow currently check for an acknowledged token window on resume vs new generation? I remember a race where session_offset is taken from the last flushed write, not last sent chunk. That could be earlier than what the client had received.

Ken L: Repro script I used (local, simulates abrupt close then resume):
```bash
# start streaming
curl -N -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -H "Idempotency-Key: ik-test" \
  "https://api.redwood.test/v1/streams?model=test" --data-raw $'{"prompt":"hello","stream":true}' \
  | sed -n '1,2p' &
# simulate network drop
sleep 0.5; pkill -9 curl
# reconnect with resume token we captured
curl -N -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -H "Idempotency-Key: ik-test" \
  "https://api.redwood.test/v1/streams?model=test&resume_token=rt-test" --data-raw $'{"prompt":"hello","stream":true}'
```
I can reproduce the duplicate token_index=1 emitted again.

Ken L: Root cause: resume uses `last_flushed_offset` (persisted asynchronously) and not `last_sent_offset`. If the last chunk was in-flight in the TCP buffer, client saw it but server didn't update flushed offset. On reconnect we resume from flushed offset and re-emit the in-flight chunk. Billing records created on chunk send + on done cause duplicate charge.

Ajay P: Two questions: can billing dedupe retroactively? And do we need to treat `idempotency-key` + `session_id` pair as canonical to suppress resumed duplicates?

Maria C: I'll collect the customer's exact timestamps and request logs for billing reconciliation. Customer OK with a 48h fix window if we provide a workaround.

Ken L: Proposed fixes:
- Short-term: change billing to only invoice on `done` for affected customer tiers to avoid double-charges (config flip).
- Mid-term: runtime change to persist `last_sent_offset` synchronously for resumed sessions or maintain an in-memory ACK map per session so resume checks the highest token index ACKed by client.
- Also, enforce resume validation: require `Idempotency-Key` on resume and treat duplicate (session_id + idempotency-key + token_range) as no-op.

Ajay P: For reproduction, add this to test matrix: flaky network tests with partial TCP flushes + resume. Add a unit test asserting no overlapping token emissions when resume_token points to an earlier offset but client already received later tokens.

Finance Bot: @Sophie R please attach charge IDs and invoice numbers so billing can triage duplicate charges.

Sophie R: Will do. I've opened ENG ticket INF-4821 and tagged `eng-runtime` with logs and repro script. Escalating billing separately. Customer wants periodic updates; I'm sending timeline and mitigation steps. :thumbsup:

Ken L: I'll push a small guard today that checks `resume_token` versus last seen `token_index` in session store and refuses a naive resume if it would re-emit already-delivered tokens. That should reduce duplicates while we implement full fix.

Sophie R: Thanks team. I'll follow up with customer and confirm the temporary billing hold for the duplicate charges.

Ajay P: +1 on test coverage. We'll need a regression test before release.

Sophie R: Closing loop once billing confirms refund/hold.
